== Biography ==
Mary Ann was born in 1816. She passed away in 1872.  Her [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/93407890/mary-ann-mcclellan record in FindAGrave] includes an interesting letter. The letter was written by Mary Ann to her sister, [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2161 Nancy Clementine Glasgow].

== Research Notes ==
=== Abbeville family records — 4 November 2026 ===

The published register matches Mary Ann’s 11 June 1816 birthday and 11 December 1833 marriage to [[McClellan-1351|John P. McClellan]]. The estate abstract names Mary McClelan among James Glasgow’s children with [[Glasgow-802|Jane Burdit]] and [[Glasgow-2161|Nancy Hunter]]. Select [[Glasgow-803|James Glasgow]] as her father at '''96% confidence''' and [[Morrow-3682|Margaret Morrow]] as her mother at '''94%'''. These are new parent recommendations. The copied letter to Nancy confirms the sister network; the maternal identification uses the family-register sequence and accompanying parent account, not a mother named in the will.<ref name="GlasgowFamilyBible">Nancy McClellan Feroe, [http://www.tngenweb.org/rutherford/glascow.html The Bible Record of James Glasgow] (2005), transcription from a photocopy sent by Oscar “Pet” Hunter on 20 February 1979. James Glasgow/Margaret Morer (Morrow) marriage, 27 February 1810; Maria Ann, Jane El. and Nancy C. births and McClellan, Burditt and Hunter marriages. The deaths are expressly separately copied family notes, not Bible entries. Original and photocopy uninspected.</ref><ref name="GlasgowEstate1847">[https://genealogytrails.com/scar/pickens/wills_1.htm Wills and Estates Notices], James Glasgow section: Abbeville will dated 12 February 1847 and equity proceedings, October–November 1851, naming Mary McClelan, Jane Burdit and Nancy Hunter among six children. The page attributes the estate material to G. Anne Sheriff, The Carolina Herald and Newsletter, Summer 2005, pp.31–39, Pauline Young Collection. Published abstracts inspected; originals uninspected. Its 1848 death conflicts with the separately copied 1849 family note.</ref><ref name="GlasgowLetter1848">[https://www.argenweb.net/bradley/bios/johnpatton/aqwg01.htm Descendants of John Patton McClellan], published Mary Anne Glasgow McClellan letter to sister Nancy Clementine Glasgow Hunter, 17 September 1848; copy attributed to Hal Glasgow, original reportedly held by Pet Hunter on 20 December 1965. The letter body refers to an unnamed father and deceased mother; explicit parent names are supplied by the accompanying genealogy. Original uninspected; the Hunter-family provenance may overlap the Bible copy.</ref>

Published transcriptions/abstracts inspected, not the Bible, its 1979 photocopy, the will/equity manuscripts or the letter original. The Bible and letter travel through the Hunter family and their online genealogies may be dependent; they are not three independent primary witnesses. James’s inherited 1788 birth conflicts with the Bible page heading’s 1778, and the estate abstract’s 1848 death conflicts with separately copied 1849 death notes. These vital questions and his own [[Glasgow-804|James Glasgow]] father remain separate. No census row, birth year, death year, Scottish ancestry or Thomas M Glasgow identity is reassigned.

The profile dates for James are not corrected from the conflicting years alone. [[Glasgow-3766|Thomas M Glasgow]] remains an unselected comparison: the Bible’s James M/N and the letter’s “Tom” are not automatically his identity. The original estate file and Bible photocopy are the next checks.
